text: I suppose the main reason is time. Once people have a full-time job and a family, learning something new tends to slip down their list of priorities. There's also a psychological side — a lot of adults are afraid of looking foolish, especially if they're used to being good at their job. That fear of being a beginner again can be a real barrier.

tips.en: A practical reason and a psychological one — deeper than just “no time”.
tips.kk: Практикалық және психологиялық себеп — жауап «уақыт жоқтан» тереңірек.
tips.ru: Практическая причина и психологическая — ответ глубже, чем «нет времени».

tips.en: The last sentence sums the idea up in one clear statement.
tips.kk: Соңғы сөйлем ойды бір ауқымды тұжырымға жинайды.
tips.ru: Последняя фраза собирает мысль в одно ёмкое утверждение.
tips.example: That fear of being a beginner again can be a real barrier

note.en: A vivid way to say “becomes less important”.

phrases.text: slip down their list of priorities

questions.question: Why do some adults stop learning new skills?

text: It really depends on the skill. For something practical like cooking, I think you can get surprisingly far on your own, with videos and a bit of trial and error. But for skills where mistakes can become habits — say, playing an instrument or driving — having a teacher from the start is much safer, because it's far harder to unlearn bad habits later.

tips.en: It depends followed by two explained examples — analysis, not avoidance.
tips.kk: It depends және бірден түсіндірмесі бар екі мысал — сұрақтан қашу емес, талдау.
tips.ru: It depends и сразу два примера с объяснением — не уход от вопроса, а анализ.
tips.example: It really depends on the skill

tips.en: A comparative with far makes the argument strong.
tips.kk: Far бар салыстырмалы шырай дәлелді күшті етеді.
tips.ru: Сравнительная степень с far делает довод сильным.
tips.example: it's far harder to unlearn bad habits later

questions.followUp: How did you learn your skills?
questions.question: Is it better to learn a skill from a teacher or by yourself?

text: Probably the ability to keep learning, to be honest. Technology is changing so fast that many specific skills people learn today might be out of date in ten years. So I'd say adaptability, along with communication skills, will matter more than any single technical ability — machines can do a lot, but they can't really build trust with other people.

tips.en: Probably and might show the right caution when talking about the future.
tips.kk: Probably және might — болашақ туралы айтқанда дұрыс сақтық.
tips.ru: Probably и might — правильная осторожность, когда говорим о будущем.
tips.example: might be out of date in ten years

tips.en: The answer ends with a clear conclusion and an unexpected point about trust.
tips.kk: Жауап анық қорытындымен және сенім туралы күтпеген дәлелмен аяқталады.
tips.ru: Ответ заканчивается ясным выводом и неожиданным доводом про доверие.

title.en: A conclusion with So I’d say

questions.followUp: How can schools prepare children for that?
questions.question: What skills do you think will be most important in the future?

text: I think they should, at least for skills related to the job. It's in their own interest, because better-trained staff work more efficiently and are less likely to leave. Some companies worry that they'll pay for a course and then the employee will move to a competitor. But in my experience, people tend to stay loyal to employers who invest in them.

tips.en: It's in their own interest is an argument the employer will understand.
tips.kk: It's in their own interest — жұмыс берушінің өзіне түсінікті дәлел.
tips.ru: It's in their own interest — довод, понятный самому работодателю.

tips.en: Some companies worry, but names the counter-argument and answers it.
tips.kk: Some companies worry … But … — қарсы дәлелді атап, бірден жауап бересіз.
tips.ru: Some companies worry … But … — называете довод против и сразу отвечаете.

questions.question: Should employers pay for their staff to learn new skills?

text: In terms of access, definitely. Thirty years ago, if you wanted to learn photography or coding, you needed a teacher or expensive books, whereas now there are free tutorials for almost everything. On the other hand, it's harder to stay focused, because there's so much choice and so many distractions. So learning has become easier to start but harder to finish.

tips.en: In terms of access, definitely says yes, but only in one sense.
tips.kk: In terms of access, definitely — «иә», бірақ тек бір мағынада.
tips.ru: In terms of access, definitely — «да», но только в одном смысле.

tips.en: Easier to start but harder to finish ends with a neat contrast.
tips.kk: Easier to start but harder to finish — қарама-қарсы қою арқылы қорытынды.
tips.ru: Easier to start but harder to finish — вывод-противопоставление.
tips.example: easier to start but harder to finish

note.en: “A lot of things that take your attention away”.
